newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukrainian miners picket parliament for pay.
newsitem.headline: Ukrainian miners picket parliament for pay.

text.p: Thousands of impoverished Ukrainian miners picketed parliament on Tuesday demanding back wages, support for their ailing industry and an end to pit closures.
They bashed their faded red hard-hats on the ground to express their disgust at not being paid for months as deputies met inside to set the agenda to mid-year.
"Wages! Pensions!" shouted the crowd of about 2,000 which had travelled mostly from the former Soviet republic's Donbass coal-producing region in the east.
The miners, depressed by the gradual decline of their once mighty industry and going months without pay, want their plight to be taken into account in this year's budget.
They want parliament to approve funds to reduce a back payments mountain which a parliamentary official has put at at 3.9 billion hryvnias ($2.1 billion).
But President Leonid Kuchma is trying to get a budget passed which will satisfy the International Monetary Fund, paving the way for a new multi-billion dollar credit.

Output at Ukraine's mines, many of which were developed at the turn of the century, has fallen gradually ever since the Soviet Union fell apart from a peak of 200 million tonnes a year to about 70 million tonnes last year.
A total of about 50 out of Ukraine's 270 pits are to be closed by 2000 and the more profitable mines modernised with the help of part of a $300 million World Bank credit.
Miners were once among the best-paid workers in the former Soviet Union, in recognition of the great need for coal in its sprawling industries.
Much of the equipment is now outdated and hundreds of miners are killed each year in accidents underground.
One miner was killed and six taken to hospital with carbon monoxide poisoning after a fire at "Chernomorka" pit in Ukraine's eastern Lugansk region late on Monday, Russia's Interfax news agency said.
